The bug is in `org.apache.commons.lang3.time.FastDateParser.NumberStrategy.addRegex(org.apache.commons.lang3.time.FastDateParser, java.lang.StringBuilder)`.

Why:
- The failing case is pattern `"M E"` with input `"3  Tue"`.
- `SimpleDateFormat` rejects this input, so FastDateParser should also reject it.
- But FastDateParser builds a regex that accepts it:
  - numeric month `M` becomes `(\p{IsNd}++)`
  - the literal space in the pattern is compiled by the quoted/literal strategy as flexible whitespace
  - day name `E` becomes `(Fri|Friday|Mon|Monday|...|Tue|Tuesday|...)`
- The failure message already exposes the generated regex:
  - `(\p{IsNd}++)\s*+(Fri|Friday|Mon|Monday|Sat|Saturday|Sun|Sunday|Thu|Thursday|Tue|Tuesday|Wed|Wednesday)`
- That regex is too permissive for `"M E"` because it accepts multiple spaces between the month and weekday, so `"3  Tue"` parses when it should fail.

Relevant static evidence:
- `FastDateParser.init()` wires strategies and builds the parse regex.
- `getStrategy("M")` returns `NUMBER_MONTH_STRATEGY` for single-letter `M`.
- `NumberStrategy.addRegex()` does:
  - exact-width digits only when the next field is numeric
  - otherwise `(\p{IsNd}++)`
- For `"M E"`, the next field is text (`E`), so it takes the permissive branch.

Root cause:
- `NumberStrategy.addRegex()` makes numeric parsing depend on whether the next field is numeric, but for a numeric field followed by a literal separator and then text, this produces an over-lenient regex and allows invalid spacing.

The dynamic verification tool was inconclusive due debugger/session failure, but the static evidence and the emitted regex in the assertion message strongly confirm this diagnosis.

m39.content:
The bug is in `org.apache.commons.lang3.time.FastDateParser.NumberStrategy.addRegex(org.apache.commons.lang3.time.FastDateParser, java.lang.StringBuilder)`.

Why:
- The failing case is pattern `"M E"` with input `"3  Tue"`.
- `SimpleDateFormat` rejects this input, so FastDateParser should also reject it.
- But FastDateParser builds a regex that accepts it:
  - numeric month `M` becomes `(\p{IsNd}++)`
  - the literal space in the pattern is compiled by the quoted/literal strategy as flexible whitespace
  - day name `E` becomes `(Fri|Friday|Mon|Monday|...|Tue|Tuesday|...)`
- The failure message already exposes the generated regex:
  - `(\p{IsNd}++)\s*+(Fri|Friday|Mon|Monday|Sat|Saturday|Sun|Sunday|Thu|Thursday|Tue|Tuesday|Wed|Wednesday)`
- That regex is too permissive for `"M E"` because it accepts multiple spaces between the month and weekday, so `"3  Tue"` parses when it should fail.

Relevant static evidence:
- `FastDateParser.init()` wires strategies and builds the parse regex.
- `getStrategy("M")` returns `NUMBER_MONTH_STRATEGY` for single-letter `M`.
- `NumberStrategy.addRegex()` does:
  - exact-width digits only when the next field is numeric
  - otherwise `(\p{IsNd}++)`
- For `"M E"`, the next field is text (`E`), so it takes the permissive branch.

Root cause:
- `NumberStrategy.addRegex()` makes numeric parsing depend on whether the next field is numeric, but for a numeric field followed by a literal separator and then text, this produces an over-lenient regex and allows invalid spacing.

The dynamic verification tool was inconclusive due debugger/session failure, but the static evidence and the emitted regex in the assertion message strongly confirm this diagnosis.
